title: Essential Python libraries and their creators

spans.text: Start with Python's standard library: pathlib handles paths, json data exchange, csv table files, sqlite3 local databases, math and statistics calculations, and asyncio I/O-heavy waiting. The standard library is maintained by Python contributors, not one inventor. Install third-party packages inside a virtual environment. NumPy supports array computing, pandas tabular data, FastAPI HTTP APIs, and Django larger web applications. Travis Oliphant and the open-source community helped create NumPy; Adrian Holovaty and Simon Willison began Django to support newsroom work; Sebastián Ramírez created FastAPI. Before choosing a package, check its license, security updates, and supported Python versions.

spans.code:
import json
from pathlib import Path

record = {"name": "Ada", "score": 10}
text = json.dumps(record)
Path("student.json").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
print(text)

spans.text: json.dumps converts a Python value to JSON text; pathlib handles the file path portably.

spans.title: Important tip
spans.text: Start with the standard library; for the examples, run `python -m pip install numpy fastapi` in the active `.venv` and record dependencies.

spans.title: Important detail
spans.text: The standard library ships with Python. External packages such as NumPy, pandas, Django, and FastAPI must be installed and tracked as project dependencies.

spans.title: Warning
spans.text: Install packages in the project's .venv, keep secrets out of source code, and review third-party package provenance.
